question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` intentionally require canonical unsigned decimal spelling and reject previously accepted `+500` and zero-padded equivalents?
rationale: The current behavior does not change the requested cadence, the public docs do not specify canonical spelling, and choosing stricter syntax intentionally breaks an accepted CLI input contract.

options.title: Preserve equivalent spellings
options.body: Keep `+500` and zero-padded digit strings compatible because they select the same interval and no current contract marks them invalid.

options.title: Adopt canonical-only syntax
options.body: Approve the breaking validation rule, document the exact grammar, and require supported-Node before/after/control CLI proof before merge.

options.title: Close as unnecessary
options.body: Close the PR if maintainers do not want a new canonical-spelling policy because the reported inputs do not alter the resulting cadence.

recommendation.title: Preserve equivalent spellings
recommendation.body: Keep `+500` and zero-padded digit strings compatible because they select the same interval and no current contract marks them invalid.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a user-visible CLI compatibility choice rather than a mechanical parser repair, and this person is the strongest available product-direction routing candidate from the discussion.
